justification: A production write to the table that is the product's differentiator, and the direction of risk is asymmetric: a WRONG link would let a later automated check compare a number against someone else's clause and report a confident false verdict, which is worse than the current state of no link at all. Small in row count (34) but it establishes a relationship other code will trust.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/link_controls_to_provisions.py   # dry-run, writes nothing; plus: python -m pytest tests/test_controls_provision_links.py -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Predicted BEFORE the final write: 13 rows updated (10 new links + 3 stale links cleared), 0 skipped by the guard, 42 linked in total afterwards. All matched. It fails if any link is dangling (0; the FK blocks it), crosses to a different council (0), points at a superseded or non-actionable provision (0), if the pre-existing human link on control 3 was changed (it was preserved; provision 98149 is current), or if a linked control's quote is absent from its linked provision text (41 of 42 present; the exception is control 3, whose link a different method made). Re-running plans 0 writes, which is the idempotency check. The suite fails if the matcher links on zero matches, on several matches, or on a quote under 30 characters.

pre_impl.existing_data: All 1,069 controls and all 505 provision document_ids read, not sampled. Confirmed from information_schema that provision_id is a nullable integer with a real FK to regulatory_provisions(id), and that dcp_setback_controls.lga is an lga_registry.slug via FK fk_dcp_setback_lga. Heaviest per-council provision fetch (Waverley, 2,965 rows) measured at 0.86s, so no batching is needed. Verified by grep that nothing in the frontend or Python reads provision_id, so no served output can change.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The task assumed linking was a matching problem. It is a coverage problem: 14 of 30 control LGAs have ZERO provisions ingested (450 controls) and a further 545 sit in councils whose specific chapter was never ingested, so only 41 of 1,069 are linkable at all. Second: source_council does not consistently hold the slug — only 16 of 30 match exactly, so resolution goes through lga_registry.display_name. Third: restricting candidates to current, actionable provisions IMPROVED the result rather than narrowing it, because it removes superseded duplicates of the same clause — ambiguity fell 23 to 2 and linkable rose 35 to 41. Fourth: the initial post-write verification reported 14 of 35 quotes present because it compared un-normalised SQL text; re-run with the matcher's own normalisation it was 34 of 35. The check was wrong, not the links.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No existing linker. scripts/validate_controls_provenance.py (#866) classifies provenance but writes nothing; it is extended here to report link coverage rather than duplicated. The safety shape (dry-run default, backup table, per-row optimistic guard, printed rollback, 30s timeout) is copied from scripts/retag_applicability_slug_docids.py and scripts/backfill_invalid_zone_codes.py. The lga -> source_council resolution reuses the lga_registry approach from #854 instead of a new hand-written map.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The only external source is the Supabase connection. No DATABASE_URL exits 2 with an explicit 'nothing was checked, which is not a pass' message rather than reporting a clean plan. Any exception during planning or writing is caught, the transaction is rolled back, and the exit code is 2 — so a partial write cannot be mistaken for success. The backup table is created and its row count compared against the plan BEFORE the first UPDATE, and the run aborts if it is smaller. There is no third-party API and no network call beyond the database.
pre_impl.frontend_type: None. provision_id is not read anywhere in frontend-nextjs or Python — verified by grep across *.ts, *.tsx and *.py before writing, which is why this write cannot change served output. If it is surfaced later the type is `number | null` at every boundary, because 1,034 of 1,069 rows are legitimately NULL and always will be for councils absent from the corpus; any consumer that assumes a link exists would be wrong for 97% of the table.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: No user-visible failure today, since nothing renders the column. The failure this design guards against is future and severe: if a wrong link were written, a later automated check would compare a control's number against someone else's clause and could report a confident 'this value does not match its source' — or worse, silently confirm a wrong number as verified. That is the fabricated-verdict class from DQ-36 applied to the controls table, which is why only exact single matches link and why 553 rows are deliberately left NULL rather than linked on a best guess.

functions.name: find_single_match
functions.input: a normalised quote and the list of (provision_id, normalised_text) pairs for that council
functions.output: the provision id only when exactly one provision contains the quote, plus the raw hit count
functions.if_none: returns None for zero matches, for several matches, and for a quote under 30 characters — the caller cannot tell the difference and cannot link on any of them

functions.name: classify
functions.input: the same quote and provision list, for one control
functions.output: exactly one outcome name, so the reported counts always sum to the table size
functions.if_none: an empty provision list returns council_has_no_provisions, which is deliberately distinct from no_provision_contains_the_quote — that distinction is the finding of this work

functions.name: quoted_clause
functions.input: a control's raw source_text, which may carry an appended citation
functions.output: the part that should appear verbatim in the provision, lowercased and whitespace-collapsed
functions.if_none: None or empty yields an empty string, which fails the length floor and so can never link

functions.name: build_plan
functions.input: an open cursor; reads every control and, per council, that council's provisions
functions.output: the rows to write plus the full outcome breakdown including rows deliberately left NULL
functions.if_none: an empty plan writes nothing, and the script is dry-run by default so a wrong plan cannot reach the database without an explicit flag

functions.name: longest_run_fraction
functions.input: a control's quote and one provision's word list
functions.output: the longest contiguous shared word-run as a fraction of the quote's length — 1.0 when the sentence is present, 0.0 when it is absent
functions.if_none: an empty quote or an empty provision returns 0.0 rather than dividing by zero, so a row with nothing to compare reads as absent, never as verbatim

functions.name: band_for
functions.input: a single run fraction between 0.0 and 1.0, produced by longest_run_fraction for one control against its best candidate provision
functions.output: exactly one of four named bands, so every measured row lands in one state
functions.if_none: there is no None branch — the final threshold is 0.0, so a fraction always names a band; a collapsed banding function is caught by the test asserting all four are reachable

functions.name: chapter_tokens
functions.input: either a control's source_chapter_key such as 'chapter-f-dev-category' or a provision's document_id such as 'Inner_West_Ashfield_DCP_2016__chapter_f_dev_category'
functions.output: comparable tokens with council name, instrument and year stripped, so the two vocabularies can be tested against each other
functions.if_none: None or empty yields an empty set, which is a subset of everything — so measure() branches on the empty case FIRST and records no_chapter_key instead of a false chapter_ingested

values.value: dcp_setback_controls.provision_id for 13 rows — 10 set from NULL, 3 cleared to NULL
values.read_at: planning time from the control row, then re-asserted by the UPDATE guard at write time
values.if_missing: the guard is `provision_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM %s` against the planned previous value; a plain equality guard would skip every row whose previous value is NULL, which is most of them. An earlier version also asserted `AND provision_id IS NULL`, which had to be removed once clearing a stale link required writing over a non-NULL id — a NULL-only guard would have silently skipped exactly the rows that most needed fixing.

queries.purpose: read one council's provisions so a control's quote can be matched against them
queries.where_clause: WHERE p.is_current AND p.v2_is_actionable AND (p.source_council = %s OR lower(p.source_council) = lower(r.display_name) OR lower(replace(p.source_council,' ','_')) = %s), joined to lga_registry with r.is_active. The currency filter is required, not optional: without it the first run linked 3 controls to a superseded provision. All three council forms are needed because only 16 of 30 control LGAs match source_council exactly. Scoped to one council per execution, so a control can never match another council's clause — verified post-write with 0 cross-council links. The UPDATE is separately scoped WHERE id = %s AND provision_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM the planned previous value.

break_it.scenario: A control is linked to the nearest or best-scoring provision, so a later check compares its number against the wrong clause and reports a confident false verdict.
break_it.what_happens: Only an exact single substring match links. Zero matches, several matches and a too-short quote all return None, and each is reported as its own outcome rather than being quietly rounded into a link.
break_it.how: Substring containment, not similarity — there is no score and no threshold. Three tests drive the refusal directions independently.

break_it.scenario: The run overwrites a human-made link with a machine guess.
break_it.what_happens: It would have. The dry run showed control 3 (already pointing at provision 98149) being re-pointed to 97850, because the same clause exists as more than one provision row. Found by inspecting the plan for non-NULL previous values before applying.
break_it.how: PRESERVE_EXISTING_LINKS keeps the human's link and counts the disagreement, and the UPDATE carries AND provision_id IS NULL so even a stale plan cannot clobber one. Verified post-write: control 3 still points at 98149.

break_it.scenario: Every row fails to match because the extractor's appended citation is not in the provision text, making the ceiling look far worse than it is.
break_it.what_happens: The trailing citation is stripped before matching. Without that the linkable count collapses and the wrong conclusion gets drawn about corpus coverage.
break_it.how: A non-citation parenthetical is deliberately KEPT, so stripping cannot widen matching and link something wrong — under-match rather than over-strip.

break_it.scenario: The council resolution silently matches nothing, so every control is reported as unlinkable and the ceiling is blamed on ingestion when it is really a join bug.
break_it.what_happens: Caught in the pre-impl audit: only 16 of 30 lga slugs equal source_council, so a single-form join would have reported 30 of 30 councils as empty. Resolution goes through lga_registry.display_name.
break_it.how: council_has_no_provisions is counted separately from no_provision_contains_the_quote, so a join bug would show as ALL councils empty rather than hiding inside a single number.

break_it.scenario: A link points at a provision belonging to a different council.
break_it.what_happens: Structurally impossible — provisions are fetched per council and matched only within that set. Verified anyway after the write: 0 cross-council links, 0 dangling links.
break_it.how: The FK to regulatory_provisions(id) additionally makes a dangling id impossible at the database level.
break_it.repro: see DQ-38 in .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md for the verification queries

break_it.scenario: Link coverage becomes a gate, so pushes fail because a council was never ingested rather than because anything is broken.
break_it.what_happens: Coverage is advisory in validate_controls_provenance.py and never affects an exit code. 450 controls belong to councils with no provisions at all, so requiring a link would fail on absent corpus.
break_it.how: The exit code still depends solely on the unverifiable count from #866.
break_it.repro: python scripts/validate_controls_provenance.py --quiet   # exit 0 with 35 of 1069 linked

break_it.scenario: The post-write verification passes vacuously and nobody notices the links are wrong.
break_it.what_happens: The first verification query reported only 14 of 35 quotes present, which looked like 21 bad links. It compared un-normalised SQL text while the matcher normalises whitespace; re-run correctly it is 34 of 35. The verification was wrong, not the links.
break_it.how: The check now reuses the script's own normalise() and quoted_clause() so it tests the same question the write answered.
break_it.repro: the discrepancy and its resolution are recorded in DQ-38

break_it.scenario: A control is linked to a SUPERSEDED clause, so a later automated check compares a live number against withdrawn text.
break_it.what_happens: It happened. The first run wrote 3 links to Marrickville provision 102098 (is_current=False) because the candidate set was not filtered. Found by measuring link currency after the write rather than assuming it.
break_it.how: The candidate query now requires p.is_current AND p.v2_is_actionable, and any existing link pointing outside that set is re-pointed or cleared. Verified post-write: 0 links to a superseded provision.

break_it.scenario: A stale link is silently RETAINED because the row no longer matches anything current.
break_it.what_happens: It would have. Staleness was only handled inside the `linkable` branch, and all 3 affected rows fell into no_provision_contains_the_quote instead — so the repair pass skipped precisely the rows it existed to fix.
break_it.how: Staleness is now tested BEFORE the outcome branch, and a stale link with no current match is CLEARED rather than kept. Verified: controls 1, 2 and 6 are now NULL.

break_it.scenario: The backup does not cover the rows about to change, so the printed rollback cannot undo the run.
break_it.what_happens: It did not. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kept the earlier run's table and the count check passed spuriously — 34 >= 13, while covering none of the 10 new rows.
break_it.how: The guard now asserts every planned id is present in the backup, not just a row count. Demonstrated firing before the real run: '10 planned rows missing', abort before any UPDATE.

post_merge.db_reset: Already applied in two runs. Final state: 42 linked of 1,069. The second run wrote 13 rows (10 new links, 3 stale links cleared), 0 skipped. Backups: dcp_setback_controls_provlink_backup_20260802b (13 rows, this run) and dcp_setback_controls_provlink_backup_20260802 (34 rows, restores the pre-any-change state). Rollback SQL is printed by the script and recorded in DQ-38.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run `python scripts/validate_controls_provenance.py` and confirm 534 / 535 / 0 with exit 0 plus 'machine-checkable (linked to a provision): 42'. Then run `python scripts/link_controls_to_provisions.py` and confirm 41 linkable, 41 already correct and 0 rows to write — that is the idempotency check.
